newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA'S BOWLERS FIGHT BACK AGAINST INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA'S BOWLERS FIGHT BACK AGAINST INDIA.

text.p: South Africa's fast bowlers seized back the initiative to reduce India to 72 for five at lunch on the second day of the first test at Kingsmead on Friday.
New ball duo Allan Donald and Shaun Pollock took two wickets apiece on a pitch offering both pace and bounce as India began shakily in reply to South Africa's first innings of 235 all out.

The key wicket of the morning session was that of Indian captain Sachin Tendulkar who, having dispatched Donald for successive fours, was comprehensively beaten the very next ball by a rapid off-cutter to be bowled through the gate for 15.

Former captain Mohammad Azharuddin then threatened an innings of arrogant aggression before top-edging a pull off all-rounder Brian McMillan and he was caught on the deep backward square leg boundary for a run-a-ball 15.
The not out batsmen at lunch were Rahul Dravid (on five) and Nayan Mongia (four) but they face a tall task if they are to help India avoid a significant first innings deficit.
The day began promisingly for the home side when Indian opener Woorkeri Raman was removed by the seventh ball of the session - and the first of the morning from fast bowler Pollock.
With India still on their overnight score of two, Raman lost his middle stump as he played across the line of a full length inswinger and he departed without scoring.

Raman's opening partner Vikram Rathore, decidedly uncomfortable against the pace of Donald, then perished seven overs later. Rathore, on seven, edged a short lifter from Donald low to third slip where Andrew Hudson took a good catch.
Tendulkar and Saurav Ganguly then batted with commendable restraint in adding 14 for the third wicket before Ganguly, on 16, produced a shot completely out of character half an hour before lunch.
The 24-year-old left-hander from Calcutta pulled at a shortish ball from Pollock and the steepling top edge was neatly taken by Lance Klusener at long leg.
